entities.summary: Psusennes II, the last king of the Twenty-first Dynasty of Egypt, ruled from approximately 987 to 944 BCE. His reign was marked by significant political and military developments, including the rise of the Egyptian Empire and the expansion of its borders. Psusennes II's military campaigns against the Libyans and the Nubians were successful, and he established trade relationships with neighboring countries. He also oversaw the construction of several temples and monuments, including the Temple of Amon at Thebes. Psusennes II's legacy extended beyond his own lifetime, as his successors continued to rule Egypt for centuries. As the Pharaoh of Egypt, Psusennes II played a crucial role in shaping the country's history and leaving a lasting impact on its people. The discovery of Psusennes II's tomb has shed new light on the life and reign of this enigmatic pharaoh, providing valuable insights into ancient Egyptian culture and politics.
